findings.finding: The arch top reads as a flat lintel with a slight shoulder rather than a pointed Gothic arch at 1x, so it does not echo the pointed windows of the existing chipset.
findings.fix: Step the inner dark opening up 1px per column toward the centre over the top 3 rows so it forms a 2-3px apex, and put a 1px light keystone pixel at the apex.

findings.finding: On the bottom (floor) row the light stone handrails and newels outweigh the treads, so the tread/riser rhythm fades exactly where the walker enters.
findings.fix: Darken the riser line under each bottom-row tread by one palette step, and drop the newel caps 1px lower or one tone darker so the treads lead.

findings.finding: The light rim runs all the way around, including a bar on the south side as thick as the others, so the stairwell reads as a closed framed box (a floor grate, vent or fireplace insert) rather than a hole open to the south. At 1x next to the sprite it looks like a wall plaque or fireplace. The entrance side is not obvious.
findings.fix: Remove the south rim bar across the inner 2 columns of each tile: replace it with the first tread nosing in light stone, flush with the room floor, with no outline under it. Keep newel posts only at the SW and SE corners and let the floor flagstones run straight into the first tread.

findings.finding: The four descending treads are near-black grey stripes with almost no value change, so nothing reads as steps going down. It reads as an empty dark slot.
findings.fix: Give each tread a 1px light nosing (2 steps above the tread colour) on its north edge, and make the treads step down in value: T1 is floor value -1, then T2 -2, T3 -3, and T4 merges into the dark north inner wall. Make the inner north wall a solid 2-3px darkest band so the descent ends in shadow.

findings.finding: The equal-height oak planks with dark gaps sit inside a dark iron frame and could at first read as a shelf or wardrobe front.
findings.fix: Shorten the upper tread tops by 1px per step going north, and add a 1px dark riser shadow under each tread's front edge that is distinct from the gap colour.

findings.finding: The timber frame and oak steps share the bookshelf wood tones, so in place the stair blends into the flanking shelves.
findings.fix: Use a darker timber tone and a 1px darkest outline on the frame posts where they meet the shelves, and raise the warm light on the top two treads by one palette step.

findings.finding: The pale grey stone treads have weak tread/riser contrast, and the single white dropping pixel reads as noise.
findings.fix: Darken the risers by two steps, add a 1px mid-grey shadow under each nosing, and replace the lone white pixel with a 2px off-white and grey splat.

findings.finding: This has the same problem as castle-stair-down: the full stone rim, including the south side, inside wooden rails makes a closed framed box that reads like a fireplace or hatch. The treads are unreadable dark stripes, and the straw speck does not help.
findings.fix: Apply the same fix as castle-stair-down: open the south rim into a light first-tread nosing flush with the floor, give each tread a light north nosing with stepped darkening down to a darkest north wall, and keep wooden newels only at the south corners.

places.finding: In the owlery (AFTER 3x) the stairwell beside the west wall reads as a wooden-framed fireplace or crate sitting on the floor, not a way down. A player standing south of it would not know they can descend.
places.fix: Fix the owl-stair-down piece as above. Optionally add a 1px dark drop-shadow line along the inside of the west and east rails to sell the depth.

places.finding: In the clocktower the stair sits flush against the gear emblem on the wall. The overlap is clean, but the iron frame and the dark emblem disc merge at 1x.
places.fix: Leave one wall-texture column between the frame's east post and the emblem, or lighten the frame's east edge by 1px.
